SnowDistribution: Variable underfoot conditions, thin soft snow in some areas, deeper denser drifts in hollows, soft snow in boulder fields. Good visibility.  Winds 30-50 mph, gusty in the corries blowing us over on occasions.
Comment: There is still the potential for small avalanches in the Low Avalanche Category. Small avalanches in steep terrian can have serious consequenses.
WeatherInfluences: A dry day with strong to gale force South backing South-South-East winds. The freezing level will be around 900 metres.
SnowStability: Unstable windslab will continue to affect steep West through North to North-East aspects mostly above 1000 metres. These accumulations will be isolated, sometimes localised and mostly affect coire rims, gully exits, and steep banks and burn lines. On these aspects, cornices will be fragile. The avalanche hazard will be Low.
ObservedWeatherInfluences: A dry day with strong to gale force South-Easterly winds.  The freezing level at midday was around 900 metres.
ObservedSnowStability: New windslab has developed on West to North aspects mainly above 1000 metres. Although poorly bonded these accumulations are mostly isolated, and in some areas localised. Areas especially affected are steep locations such as coire rims and the tops of gullies.  The avalanche hazard is Low.
